To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
stimulation of CD3+CD4-CD8+ T lymphocyte cells with anti-CD3 monoclonal antibodies results in de novo expression of CD4 on the cells, which renders these cells susceptible to HIV infection.
activation of CD8+T cells through the T-cell receptor complex results in de novo expression of CD4 on the cell surface and in HIV infection of CD8+ cells.

(a) CD8+ T-cell activation through the T-cell receptor turns on CD8+ T-cells CD4 gene expression and leads to the appearance of double positive CD8+CD4+ T-cells that become infected by HIV; (b) CD8+CD8+ double positive T-cells from HIV-infected patients contain HIV DNA sequences and may play a role in HIV disease progression; (c) CD8+ CD4+ T-celss are susceptible to HIV
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how HIV causes AIDS.
the study of the molecular and cellular mechanisms involved in T lymphocyte activation, with special emphasis in CD8+ T-cells and HIV infection.
the mechanisms of T lymphocyte activation and the role of T lymphocytes in HIV pathogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD4 expression is induced in CD8 T cells by T cell receptor activation.
CD4 expression is induced by T-cell activation and that the CD4 molecule is not only involved in T-cell activation, but also in T-cell differentiation and maturation.
HIV infection is the cause of the AIDS syndrome and that the disease can be prevented and treated by antiviral therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD8+ T-cells can be infected by HIV and that this is the mechanism by which HIV causes immunodeficiency.
the TCR is not the only way to activate T cells.
HIV-1 is capable of infecting CD8+ T-cells in vivo and that the infection of CD8+T cells can occur through the CD4 receptor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CD8+ cells can be infected with HIV and that the infection is enhanced by the activation of CD8+ cells.
CD8+ T-cell activation through the T-cell receptor turns on the CD4 gene, leading to CD4 expression on the cell surface, which makes the cells susceptible to HIV infection.
CD8+ T-cell activation can result in the expression of CD4, the receptor for HIV.
